correctness.rationale: An adjacent unequal swap reverses inversion parity. The first unequal designated pair remains first after the swap, so exchanging it partitions all nonfixed words into disjoint graph edges without changing content. Fixed words consist of doubled letters and possibly a last singleton, and have even parity since cross-pair inversions come in fours and inversions with the singleton in twos. The edge-and-singleton partition bounds the independent set by the even side, which attains the bound. Fixed words have the required count F in each composition, and globally have q^ceil(n/2) choices. The n=1 case and zero multiplicities cause no exception. The finding treats detection, not correction.
residual_risks: The exact graph computation covers the two stated slices only; the matching proof gives the unrestricted result. The discussion of Abdel-Ghaffar's channel as necessarily joint is not established by the accessible abstract; this does not affect the audited theorem.

evidence: Kim's two-element orbits become disjoint swap edges. In a row-disjoint shape the excluded tableaux have every designated pair in one row, i.e. all such pairs of letters equal. Apply to even prefixes of odd words, keeping their final symbol fixed. In both cases the unmatched words are all even by the doubled-letter count, and their number is F in a composition.
Every independent set picks at most one vertex per matched edge plus the unmatched vertices. Thus the known matching gives (M+F)/2 directly, and summing gives the global formula.

originality.rationale: Kim's published sign-reversing involution for skew tableaux specializes to precisely the claimed adjacent-edge matching, not merely to the inversion-parity enumeration. To see this, place each symbol's copies in its own horizontal skew row, with disjoint column sets. Assign the label j to the next cell in the row prescribed by the j-th letter. Standard fillings and words of the composition are then in bijection. Kim's first pair of consecutive entries 2i−1,2i in distinct rows and columns becomes the first unequal designated pair of letters. For odd word length, fix the final symbol and apply the same even-size construction separately on each prefix slice. The parity of unmatched words and the independence bound then follow immediately, completing the exact formulas without a new structural theorem. This is broader prior coverage by reduction; it is not a claim that Kim states a detection code result.
residual_risks: The two inaccessible full texts may give direct detection or related Hamilton-path coverage. The verdict rests on the inspected exact involution and mathematical reduction, not on either retrieval failure.

value.rationale: The single-swap detection optimum is a natural quantity, but the claimed advance over classical parity enumeration is the matching certificate, and that certificate is already supplied by the same first-pair construction in a broader result. The swap-channel reformulation and counts are useful exposition, not a distinct nonroutine contribution or a new code property beyond the implication.
residual_risks: Neither the frozen theorem nor this reduction addresses one-error correction or broader error models. Correcting the characterization of the older literature would not restore a distinct theorem.
